# v0.49.35

This patch makes long OpenCode 2 sessions faster by letting OpenCode fold its own stored history while the session is idle, starts emergency recovery when OpenCode 2 reports an overflow as a failed step, keeps the context limit steady across a plugin reload, moves more `ctx_expand` work off OpenCode 2's main thread, fixes Oh My Pi turns refused after tag renumbering, and lets subagent sessions reclaim more context.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode or Pi after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Long OpenCode 2 sessions got slower with every message (#632, thanks @moynzzz):** OpenCode 2 loads a session's whole stored history on every step, and Magic Context trimmed it afterwards, so a long session paid for its full history each time. When a long session goes idle, Magic Context now asks OpenCode to fold its stored history behind a checkpoint, and OpenCode loads only what follows it. On a 25,000-message test session, a step dropped from 1.3–2.0 seconds to 0.33–0.49 seconds. What the model receives is unchanged, and so is the prompt cache.
- **Emergency recovery didn't start on an OpenCode 2 overflow (#827, thanks @tobwen):** Magic Context only noticed a "context too large" rejection when it arrived as an HTTP error. With OpenAI's Responses API, the same error can arrive inside a streamed response, which OpenCode 2 reports as a failed step. Those failed steps now start recovery too.
- **A plugin reload forced a full prompt rebuild on OpenCode (#826, thanks @iceteaSA):** after a reload, the first pass used the model's catalog limit instead of the session's proven context limit, and the smaller budget rebuilt the whole cached prompt. The proven limit is now kept across the reload. A real drop in capacity, such as a model change or an overflow, still rebuilds once.
- **`ctx_expand` still blocked OpenCode 2's main thread (#825, thanks @iceteaSA):** looking up raw message positions ran on the serving thread, and its cost grew with the session's length instead of the range expanded. Those lookups now run on a background thread, by row position, and so do range expansions. The output is unchanged.
- **Oh My Pi turns refused after tag renumbering (#778, thanks @sisttri):** with OpenAI's Responses API, a renumbered session could keep an old tag number in the stored copy of a signed reply, and Oh My Pi's dispatch check then refused every turn. Magic Context now removes that stale number from the stored copy, only on a pass that is already rebuilding the cached prompt, and replays the same decision on later passes.
- **Subagent sessions kept old tool-call skeletons (#643, thanks @dhaern):** in a subagent session, dropped tool calls outside the newest 20 now become full removals instead of short skeletons, on a pass that is already rebuilding the cached prompt. That frees more context in long subagent runs. Primary sessions are unchanged.
- **`ctx_expand` gave no useful answer for a file or image whose content wasn't kept (#780, thanks @null-axiom):** it returned only the part's name. It now says plainly that the content wasn't kept, with the file's name, type and stored location when known, and suggests asking the user to attach it again. It never prints inline file data.
- **Summaries could carry commit hashes from outside their range (#774, thanks @null-axiom):** a hash in a summary is now kept only if it appears in the messages that summary covers. Plain numbers are never treated as hashes. When a session's stored history is renumbered, inline message labels in summaries now move with it, but only when the shift is certain.

## Logging

- **Auto-search explains its decisions (#773, thanks @null-axiom):** each automatic memory search now logs one line with its outcome, the top score in each search lane, the near misses below the threshold, the search pool's state and the time taken. No query or memory text is logged.
- **Clearer logs when a summary times out (#828, thanks @dhaern):** the logs now say whi

## Dashboard v0.20.23

The Cache page keeps reading Broca runs once Broca starts recording how a run and Magic Context agreed on the shape of history edits. Without this update, those runs would stop showing their steps and usage. Works with Magic Context 0.49.x.

# v0.49.34

This patch stops OpenCode 1 sessions from ending up with two summary markers after a failed save.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **A failed save could leave a second summary marker on OpenCode 1:** when Magic Context moves the point OpenCode loads history from, it writes a marker into OpenCode's database and then records that marker in its own database. If the second write failed, the next history update didn't know the first marker was its own and added another. Magic Context now records the marker it intends to write before writing it, and the next update adopts a marker that's already in place instead of adding one. Cases it can't settle with certainty are logged and left untouched.
  - **Cleanup of leftover markers** now runs only on a pass that is already rebuilding the cached prompt, so it can never change what a cached request loads.
  - **OpenCode 2 and Pi:** unchanged. They don't use this marker.

# v0.49.33

This patch stops OpenCode 2 sessions from paying two full prompt-cache writes when their tool list changes.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **A tool-list change cost two full cache writes on OpenCode 2 (#819, thanks @iceteaSA):** when a plugin reload added, removed or renamed tools, the provider lost its cached prompt on the next request, but Magic Context treated that pass as a cache hit. Its history head stayed as it was and its queued drops stayed held, so each session paid a second full write later, when those drops finally landed. On OpenCode 2, a change to the names or descriptions of the tools a session sends now rebuilds the history head once, and the queued drops and cleanup land in that same rebuild.
  - **Upgrading:** the first pass after the upgrade records each session's tool list without rebuilding.
  - **Schema-only differences:** a change to a tool's schema alone never counts, so it can't cause a rebuild that the provider wouldn't already pay for.
  - **Known limits:** a plugin that changes the tool list after Magic Context's hook isn't seen. A tool entry that OpenCode drops before sending can still cause one rebuild when its description changes.
  - **OpenCode 1 and Pi:** unchanged. Their tool-list signal is shared by every session in the process, so it still isn't used.

# v0.49.32

This patch stops Pi's `ctx_search` from returning messages from a branch you left with `/tree`, and removes three more reads that blocked OpenCode's main thread while nothing had changed.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode or Pi after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Pi search returned messages from an abandoned branch (#807, thanks @LioTree):** after `/tree` moved to another branch and the session continued, `ctx_search` could return messages from the branch you left, once later summaries passed their message numbers. A branch change on Pi and Oh My Pi now rebuilds that session's message search index from the active branch, the same way OpenCode 2 already does after a revert. Until the rebuild finishes, message search returns no message results, and a search or automatic hint already in flight drops any message result from the old branch. Memories, notes, summaries and git results are unaffected.
- **Three OpenCode reads repeated when nothing had changed (#825, thanks @iceteaSA):**
  - **Dream backlog counts:** the sidebar recounted the dreamer's pending work on every poll, because any database write reset its cache. The sidebar and status display now reuse a count for up to 60 seconds. The dreamer's own scheduling still uses exact counts.
  - **Chunk coverage:** the check rebuilt each summary's search text from the index even when nothing in it had changed. It now reuses the previous result while the summary and its indexed messages are unchanged, and rebuilds as soon as either changes.
  - **Mis-scoped chunk scan:** every project registration, including each plugin reload, rescanned for misfiled search chunks. A finished scan is now remembered per project and embedding model, and runs again after a session's project changes.

  None of these changes what the model sees.
